label: Shakuhachi, sampled, close and dry
audition_title: libsonare shakuhachi vs the sampled reference
_notes: Every fourth semitone across the compass this program is probed on, 60 to 84, and no further. Both ends were rendered before the grid was written and both speak: the peaks run 0.177, 0.186, 0.168 at the low, middle and high probe notes, and the share of energy on the played key's own series is 0.974 or better at all three. A note outside the compass is left out rather than transposed, because there the reference is stretching a sample and a model fitted against it would be fitted against the sampler.
_velocities: Five, and the axis is timbre rather than level on anything blown. Measured at the middle probe note, velocity 32 sits -7.1 dB under velocity 100, and the soft end stays a clean tone rather than thinning into noise. The softest row is kept because it is the most distinct timbre this instrument has, not because the level is interesting.
_dry: Nothing to switch off, measured rather than assumed. With the rack loaded not one of the plugin's advertised parameters matches `reverb`, and the render agrees: the release reaches the numerical floor without a tail behind it. There is no room, so `dry` has no section to act on and is left off rather than claiming an effect was disabled. What that buys downstream is a dry anchor: every level and release measured against it is the instrument alone.
_stimulus: The metrics take their sustain window between 0.6 s and 1.8 s after onset, so the gate has to outlast that with margin. The key stops the note and nothing follows it: 100 ms after note-off the render is at the numerical floor (-159 dB). Half a second of tail records the whole of that and anything longer is silence on disk.
_calibration: From `capture.py calibrate` on this rack: the reference renders identically in real time and faster than it, the same note twice is bit-identical - so there is no round robin to put a floor under the loss - and the measured settle minimum is 250 ms. `realtime` is kept on anyway, because a note streamed late is caught only by `verify` and would otherwise be committed as a measurement.
_timbres: One, and the ladder is monotone above it, so this capture cannot move the voice past `voiced` however complete its coverage. That is a property of the source rather than of the work: the rack holds one slot per GM program, so there is no second of this instrument in it to disagree with, and `source_for` takes every timbre of a capture from one plugin, so a soundfont render cannot stand in as a second. What the reference buys is a measured target for `autofit` and `--diagnose` where the voice could previously only be fitted by ear. Adding a second timbre later is an edit to this list rather than a re-capture.
_dimensions: Nine of the ten a sustained voice can be judged on. `damper` is the load-bearing one on a wind: the note stops when the breath stops, and a model whose release is a decay rather than a stop gives itself away there before anywhere else. The slot is a air jet source, and the partial ladder `balance` reads is where that shows.
_dimensions_na: The exclusions as data, since a dimension argued only in prose reads as a gap. Coverage is read against `toneclass.canonical_dimensions`, which for a sustained voice already drops `decay`, `aftersound` and `doubling` - a voice fed continuously has no free fall for them to describe - so those are not listed here.

dimensions_na.stereo: the slot renders dual mono: the two channels are bit-identical, so the width is zero by construction rather than by voicing

_identity: Which product this is captured from lives in the untracked sibling `shakuhachi.local.json`: the plugin's component triple and the slot's preset. Everything here is the method. Re-capturing needs the overlay; scoring, fitting and diagnosing read `reference/shakuhachi.json` and need nothing.
_slots: Slot identity is measured, never taken from a name or a position. The rack is addressed by MIDI channel; this program answers on channel 14, and it was rendered at its own three probe notes before anything else was written, reading 0.974 or better of its energy on the series of the key that was pressed. That is what says the slot is a pitched instrument tracking the keyboard rather than whatever its position suggests.
